task_name: Transactional task metadata validation and workspace lock primitives [prereq]

concerns_addressed: The cumulative sequential range b2b678a67bc2fcb5dd81a7c582083aff0a7c6ba0..d4c77a1484a7e166abf03477fe239f6cafb5cbab contains exactly the six mapped T3 files and no client, schema, dependency, realtime, or open-redirect changes.

The cycle-1 threshold findings for parseProjectPhase, validateTaskCreateMetadata, lockTaskCreateReferences, and the integration fixture setup are cleared: each target function and fixture helper is now below roughly 50 lines, with responsibilities separated rather than merely moved as one oversized body.

The validator continues to use only the supplied transaction DBExecutor for status and parser-backed reference reads, aggregates deterministic field errors, returns mutationPerformed:false, and preserves Project/Phase inference and mismatch behavior.

The additive parser contract remains compatible: parseProjectPhase and parseDateRange preserve existing callers and error members, strict date-only validation remains intact, and malformed/reversed date inputs expose stable field errors without coercion.
The lock helper retains workspace-first, deterministic sorted category locks and destination-column-last ordering, with the same recording-executor coverage.

The real integration fixture remains unmocked and PostgreSQL-backed under RUN_INTEGRATION=1; the cycle-1 concern about a root aggregate forwarding path is not a T3 issue because T3 specifies server-only commands and no client forwarding test or requirement exists.
The pre-existing client open-redirect concern and unrelated client formatting are outside this cumulative T3 diff and are not implementation findings.

strengths: Field-specific validator helpers cleanly separate status, priority, labels, assignees, and Project/Phase aggregation while preserving deterministic execution and error insertion order.
parseProjectPhase now separates base validation, explicit phase handling, and project-only handling without changing its optional DBExecutor or legacy public result contract.
Lock acquisition is decomposed into category-specific helpers while preserving workspace, members, vocabularies, projects, phases, and destination ordering with sorted IDs.
The integration fixture setup is split into focused base, vocabulary, project, and aggregate setup helpers without weakening real transaction coverage or introducing mocks.
The date parser keeps strict calendar validation and legacy error text while adding additive fieldErrors for both malformed fields and reversed ranges.
The cumulative change remains exactly six server route/parser files, uses .js imports, and introduces no dependencies or schema changes.

issues.description: Accepted pre-existing file-size observation: tracker-item-parsers.ts is 373 lines in the reviewed commit, but it was already 305 lines at the b2b678a6 baseline. Per the explicit user waiver and the prohibition on expanding T3's six-file map, this threshold observation is non-blocking and requires no further refactor in T3.
